```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7,
  fig.height = 4.5, dpi = 100)
library(spax)
```

This example fits the experimental static conditional-logit (CLM) allocation
model to real, openly licensed data: where the residents of each small area in
Cornwall are registered with a GP. It then splits each area's access into two
parts:

- **reach** (ρ): the share of residents the model allocates to some practice in
  the area at all, and
- **availability** (ā): GP full-time equivalents per 1,000 of those residents,
  after accounting for everyone else who uses the same practices.

The question the split answers is whether an area's problem is getting to a
practice or what it finds when it gets there. For the method and its
assumptions, start with [Choosing an FCA index or an allocation
model](model-choice.html) and the [generated allocation
example](allocation-workflow.html).

## The data

All objects ship with spax. Their sources and licences are listed in
`system.file("COPYRIGHTS", package = "spax")`.

```{r data}
areas <- sf::st_drop_geometry(cornwall_lsoa)
gp <- sf::st_drop_geometry(cornwall_gp)
c(areas = nrow(areas), practices = nrow(gp), flows = nrow(cornwall_flows))
summary(cornwall_travel[!areas$scilly, !gp$scilly][, 1:3])
```

The Isles of Scilly have no road link to the mainland, so their travel times
to mainland practices are `NA`. This example models the mainland: 336 small
areas and 54 practices.

```{r inputs}
mainland_area <- !areas$scilly
mainland_gp <- !gp$scilly
travel <- cornwall_travel[mainland_area, mainland_gp]

# Demand: residents registered with any GP practice in England.
demand <- setNames(areas$registered[mainland_area], areas$lsoa[mainland_area])
# Supply: GP full-time equivalents, excluding GPs in training.
supply <- setNames(gp$gp_fte_extg[mainland_gp], gp$practice[mainland_gp])

# Observed flows: registered residents by small area and practice.
observed <- matrix(0, nrow(travel), ncol(travel), dimnames = dimnames(travel))
keep <- cornwall_flows$lsoa %in% rownames(travel) &
  cornwall_flows$practice %in% colnames(travel)
observed[cbind(cornwall_flows$lsoa[keep], cornwall_flows$practice[keep])] <-
  cornwall_flows$patients[keep]
c(registered = sum(demand), at_mainland_practices = sum(observed))
```

Demand counts every registered resident, wherever they are registered, so the
model's outside option corresponds to registration with a practice outside
Cornwall. It is not unmet need: almost everyone in England is registered with
some practice.

## Fit the model

The model gives each practice an attraction proportional to its GP FTE, which
decays with travel time through a Gaussian kernel with scale σ. The outside
option v0 competes with all practices. Fitting to the small area × practice
flows uses where people actually register, which identifies both parameters.

```{r fit}
inputs <- prepare_allocation(demand, supply, travel, metadata = list(
  demand_units = "registered residents", demand_period = "July 2026",
  supply_units = "GP FTE excluding GPs in training", supply_period = "June 2026",
  travel_units = "minutes"))
model <- clm_allocation(inputs, family = "gaussian", fit_v0 = TRUE)
starts <- rbind(near = c(sigma = 3, v0 = 0.05), middle = c(sigma = 6, v0 = 0.01),
  far = c(sigma = 12, v0 = 0.002))
fit <- fit_allocation(model, observed, starts,
  lower = c(sigma = 0.5, v0 = 1e-6), upper = c(sigma = 60, v0 = 10),
  output = "flow", loss = "poisson", gradient = TRUE,
  control = list(maxit = 300, factr = 10, pgtol = 1e-8))
summary(fit)
coef(fit)
```

All three starts converge away from the bounds. They stop within about 0.5% of
each other in σ and within one part in ten million in loss; the summary still
flags this as disagreement because its default tolerances are deliberately
strict, so read the gaps in its table rather than the flag alone. A σ of a few
minutes means registration is very local: a practice twice σ away keeps only
about 14% of its pull.

```{r fit-check}
fitted_totals <- colSums(fitted(fit))
cor(fitted_totals, colSums(observed))
```

## Split access into reach and availability

`evaluate_allocation()` solves the fitted model once and returns the
decomposition. Availability is judged against the Cornwall average: GP FTE per
registered patient across all mainland practices. Reach is judged against a
fixed 0.95, because almost everyone is registered and a cut at the average
reach would split areas on differences of a fraction of a percent.

```{r evaluate}
norm <- sum(supply) / sum(observed)
baseline <- evaluate_allocation(model, coef(fit), coverage_args = list(
  norm = norm, units = "GP FTE per registered patient",
  contact_cut = 0.95, adequacy_cut = norm))
cells <- as.data.frame(baseline$coverage, type = "cells")
cells$abar_per_1000 <- 1000 * cells$abar
summary(cells[, c("rho", "abar_per_1000")])
```

Reach is close to 1 almost everywhere, while availability varies several-fold
between areas. Weighting by residents shows where people live in each class:

```{r quadrants}
round(100 * tapply(cells$demand, cells$quadrant, sum) / sum(cells$demand), 1)
```

## Maps

```{r maps, fig.height = 6}
library(ggplot2)
mapped <- merge(cornwall_lsoa[mainland_area, c("lsoa", "geometry")], cells,
  by.x = "lsoa", by.y = "origin_id")
ggplot(mapped) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = abar_per_1000), colour = NA) +
  geom_sf(data = cornwall_gp[mainland_gp, ], size = 0.6) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "rocket", direction = -1,
    name = "GP FTE per\n1,000 reached") +
  labs(title = "Availability given reach") +
  theme_void()
```

Low availability concentrates in areas served by practices with large lists for
their GP staffing; reach shows almost no geographic pattern.

```{r reach-map, fig.height = 6}
ggplot(mapped) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = rho), colour = NA) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "mako", direction = -1, name = "Reach ρ") +
  labs(title = "Reach") +
  theme_void()
```

## Reading the result

- Distance decay is the most robust quantity here: σ stays within a few
  minutes under different demand definitions and travel sources.
- Reach is close to saturated by design. Registration is near-universal, and
  the outside option only captures registration elsewhere.
- Availability is the informative axis. Areas classed as capacity-limited reach
  a practice easily but share its GPs with many other patients.
- This is a single snapshot. A model in which attraction falls as practices get
  busier can fit such data better, but in GP data staffing also follows list
  size, so a snapshot cannot separate the two directions. Testing that kind of
  feedback needs supply that changes over time, such as practice closures.
